videoIdeas.title: Why your generation can't talk
videoIdeas.hook: The amount of people who can't string a sentence together in a room full of people is genuinely embarrassing.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your 'struggle to string a sentence together' post (624 views, 0 comments) hit a real nerve but got buried because the caption was long and the payoff was vague. This is your public speaking pillar — the pillar you barely post — and it's a topic nobody in your niche is owning. Package it as a punchy standalone and it becomes evergreen instead of a throwaway thought.
videoIdeas.script: The amount of people who can't string a sentence together in a room full of people is genuinely embarrassing. And before you get defensive — I'm not saying everyone needs to be a public speaker. I'm saying you should be able to hold a conversation without collapsing into 'like', 'erm', and 'you know what I mean'. Here's the uncomfortable bit: it's not a talent problem. It's a reps problem. You spend hours a day typing to people and zero minutes actually talking to them face to face. So of course your mouth freezes the second there's no keyboard between you and another human. Fix it the boring way. Talk to the shopkeeper. Speak up in the halaqah. Ask the question in the room instead of Googling it after. You don't get articulate by reading about it. You get articulate by being slightly uncomfortable, on purpose, over and over.

visuals.setting: Plain wall or masjid corridor, natural light, mid-shot, talking straight to camera with calm controlled energy — not shouting, just direct. Simple hoodie or shirt, the 'older brother pulling you aside' look.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'you sound like this ->' then a quick cut to you doing an exaggerated 'erm... like... you know...' before snapping into the real line.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open mid-sentence stumbling on purpose, then stop dead and say the hook
On-screen caption counting filler words with a tally that keeps climbing
Pattern interrupt: start silent for 2 seconds staring at camera, then hit the line

videoIdeas.title: Competent and trustworthy — in that order
videoIdeas.hook: Everyone wants to lead. Almost nobody wants to be the two things that actually make a leader.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your Al-Qawi wal-Ameen post (508 views) had a strong idea but the hook was buried under a caption. Leadership is a core pillar and this Prophetic framing is uniquely yours — competitors like daanish win on save-worthy structured advice, so give this the same clean, quotable treatment.
videoIdeas.script: Everyone wants to lead. Almost nobody wants to be the two things that actually make a leader. The Qur'an gives you the criteria in one line — Al-Qawi wal-Ameen. Strong and trustworthy. Competent and honest. And notice the order people ignore. We chase influence before character. We want the platform before we've earned the trust. But a strong man who can't be trusted is just a threat with good PR. And a trustworthy man who's useless is a nice guy nobody follows. You need both, and you build them quietly, before anyone's watching. Stop asking how to get people to follow you. Start asking whether you'd follow yourself.

visuals.setting: Slightly more composed setting — bookshelf or clean neutral background, seated, steady framing. Measured tone, this one is more teach than rant.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text: 'Al-Qawi wal-Ameen' with the two English words appearing one at a time as you say them.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on the last line 'would you follow yourself?' then cut back to the start
Two-word split screen text: STRONG / TRUSTED with an X drawn between them
Hold up a physical book/mushaf, point to it, then deliver the line

videoIdeas.title: Stop calling it self-improvement
videoIdeas.hook: Half of you aren't improving. You're just consuming content about improving and calling it the same thing.
videoIdeas.rationale: Saffana and daanish are winning with blunt contrarian takes that call the audience out ('stop writing like comic sans', 'if you're in your 20s save this'). You already do this naturally in your Ummah commentary — apply that same sharp-older-brother bluntness to the mindset pillar, which you rarely touch directly.
videoIdeas.script: Half of you aren't improving. You're just consuming content about improving and calling it the same thing. You've watched forty videos on discipline this week. You've saved three reels on your morning routine. Your notes app has a five-year plan in it. And you've done none of it. Because watching feels like progress without any of the risk of actually trying and failing. It's comfortable. It's also a trap. Here's the test — if you deleted every self-development account you follow, including this one, would your life actually get worse? Or would you finally have the silence to just start? Consume less. Do one thing badly today. That's the whole game.

visuals.setting: Casual, handheld or leaning against a wall, slightly more relaxed energy — the honest chat, not the lecture. Direct eye contact.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'this includes this account' flashes as you say 'including this one' — a self-aware jab that stops the scroll.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open scrolling a phone then locking it and looking up at camera
On-screen text punchline: 'saving ≠ doing' held on screen
Pattern interrupt: 'delete me. Seriously.' as opener, then explain

videoIdeas.title: 3 things nobody tells you about leading people
videoIdeas.hook: Nobody follows you because of your title. Here's what they actually respond to.
videoIdeas.rationale: Daanish's listicle/save format ('5 careers', 'if you're in your 20s save this') is clearly the highest-performing structure in your niche right now. You have zero list-format content. Adapt it to leadership in your blunt voice for save-and-share value you're currently missing.
videoIdeas.script: Nobody follows you because of your title. Here's what they actually respond to. One — you go first. When it's uncomfortable, when it's the hard call, when someone has to speak up. People don't follow the person who delegates the risk. They follow the one who takes it. Two — you're consistent when no one's clapping. Anyone can lead when it's exciting. Real trust is built in the boring weeks. Three — you give people credit and you eat the blame. Backwards from what most 'leaders' do. If you flip those three, you get followed. If you flip them, people just tolerate you until they don't have to.

visuals.setting: Clean neutral background, seated or standing steady, controlled and confident. Numbered on-screen text appears for each point.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text '1, 2, 3' pre-loading in the corner with the hook line over the top so people know it's a save-worthy list.
otherHookIdeas: On-screen text 'save this' subtle in corner from second one
Cold open on point 3 (the strongest) then restart from one
Count down 3-2-1 on screen instead of up to build tension

videoIdeas.title: You're not shy. You're unprepared.
videoIdeas.hook: You're not actually shy. You just walk into every room having done zero preparation and then blame your personality.
videoIdeas.rationale: Public speaking is your least-served pillar and the sentence-stringing post proved appetite exists. This reframes a common excuse ('I'm just shy/introverted') with your signature blunt refusal to let people off the hook — a format that mirrors the confrontational energy driving your top commentary videos.
videoIdeas.script: You're not actually shy. You just walk into every room having done zero preparation and then blame your personality. Think about it. The times you froze — did you actually know what you wanted to say? Or did you rock up hoping the words would arrive on their own? They don't. Confident speakers aren't born calmer than you. They've just rehearsed the first line so many times their nerves have nothing to grip onto. Before your next meeting, next presentation, next time you want to say something in the group chat's voice-note equivalent — write your opening sentence. Say it out loud three times. That's it. Half of what you call anxiety is just you being caught off guard by your own turn to speak.

visuals.setting: Standing, upright, slightly assertive posture, plain background. Energy is 'I'm calling you out but I'm right'. Direct address.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text: 'shy' with a red line struck through it, replaced by 'unprepared'.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open mid-freeze, awkward pause, then snap into the line
On-screen text punchline: 'nerves have nothing to grip onto' held on screen
Prop: hold up a sticky note with one sentence written on it as the fix

videoIdeas.title: Building beats complaining
videoIdeas.hook: While half the timeline argues online, young Muslims are quietly building cafés, study circles and actual community. Guess who wins.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your 'third spaces' post (901 views, only 2 comments) had one of your most constructive, forward-looking messages but underperformed on engagement because the caption trailed off and didn't pose anything. This is a positive-vision take that stands out against your mostly reactive feed — reframe it around a mindset lesson and add a question to drive comments.
videoIdeas.script: While half the timeline argues online, young Muslims are quietly building cafés, study circles, community hubs — actual third spaces. And guess who wins in ten years. Not the loudest account. The people who built something real. Here's the mindset shift nobody wants to hear — complaining is free, so everyone does it. Building costs you time, money, and the risk of looking stupid, so almost no one does. That's exactly why it's worth it. The scarcity is the point. You don't need permission and you don't need a platform. You need one room, a few sincere people, and the willingness to start small and ugly. So tell me — what's the one thing you'd build if you stopped waiting? Say it in the comments. Out loud counts.

visuals.setting: Out and about — filmed near a café, community space, or on the move rather than a static talking head, to match the 'building' theme. Warmer, more optimistic energy than your commentary videos.
visuals.visualHook: B-roll of a busy café / people gathered, with on-screen text 'this is a flex' over it before you appear.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open walking into a space then turning to camera
On-screen text contrast: 'arguing online' vs 'building this' with a cut
End-card question graphic to visually prompt comments

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: Your best post ever (6135 views, 211 likes) — timely, opinionated commentary on protests with a clear stance in the first line. The confrontational framing ('same people criticising... probably use it to make themselves feel better') is exactly the sharp-older-brother voice that pulls views and shares in your niche.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 15 comments on 6135 views is low for a take this divisive. The caption states a position but never asks the audience anything. End with a direct question or a line that forces people to pick a side in the comments to convert that reach into engagement and reach further.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: The 'can't string a sentence together' opener is one of your strongest, most relatable hooks and it's your only real public speaking-pillar post — a pillar competitors are ignoring. The bluntness lands.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 624 views and 0 comments — the caption runs long and buries the payoff, so there's no clear lesson or action to react to. Cut the caption to the hook plus one sharp takeaway, and give the video an actual fix people can try. This idea deserves a proper standalone (see 'Why your generation can't talk').

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: Rare constructive, forward-looking post (901 views) — celebrating young Muslims building third spaces stands out positively against your mostly reactive commentary. This vision-casting is on-brand for the mindset/leadership pillars.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 2 comments — it informs but doesn't provoke. The caption reads like a report, not a conversation. Add a direct question ('what would you build?') and tighten the opening line into a punchy claim. Positive posts still need a hook and a prompt to travel.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: Strong leadership-pillar content with a genuinely quotable idea — 'we chase influence before character' and the Al-Qawi wal-Ameen framing is unique to you and screams save-worthy. Good like ratio (58 likes on 508 views).
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 508 views and 1 comment — the concept is buried behind a book-reference caption ('📖 11 Prophetic Qualities...') that reads like a carousel, not a hook. Lead with the contrarian line as the spoken hook, structure it as a clean teachable point, and it can perform like daanish's list posts.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 828 views with 24 comments — one of your highest comment counts, proving that a short, pointed one-line caption ('Don't let sectarianism blind you...') drives more debate than your long captions do. Take note: brevity plus a firm stance works for your audience.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: The topic is heavy and risks pure argument rather than useful engagement. Keep the punchy caption style but steer the payoff toward a constructive angle so comments become discussion, not just sectarian back-and-forth — protect the account's positioning while keeping the reach.
